category_title: Non-verbal students with moderate to severe cognitive impairments who respond to modified instrumentation and social reinforcement
minimal_context: Zack is transitioning to a circle formation with his peers in a fourth-grade inclusive music class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright class, it is time to transition to our circle formation.

STUDENT: (Walks toward the circle with a girl from the class, looking around at the other fourth graders as if waiting for his captive audience to say "Good job, Zack!")

TUTOR: Keep walking to your spot in the circle.

STUDENT: (Stops walking and stretches his arms out, trying to hug the girl walking next to him.)

TUTOR: Zack, no hug. Let's just walk.

STUDENT: (When the girl touches his outstretched arms to hold him back, he ducks under her arms and hugs her anyway.)

options.A: Observe the target behavior during class and record data in scatter plots and ABC charts.
options.B: Provide a clear beginning and end for each transition and task during daily class activities.
options.C: Observe the student's interests each day and build the upcoming curriculum based on those observations.
options.D: Model acceptance and openness to the student's exceptionalities during daily class activities.
